A firewall is a network security device that monitors incoming and outgoing traffic and decides whether to allow or block specific traffic based on a defined set of security rules. Firewalls can be hardware-based, software-based, or a combination of both.

A VPN (Virtual Private Network) creates an encrypted tunnel over the public internet, allowing remote users to access private network resources securely. VPNs protect data in transit from eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.

An IDS (Intrusion Detection System) monitors network traffic for suspicious activity and known threats, generating alerts when it detects anomalies. An IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) goes a step further by actively blocking detected threats.

Zero Trust security assumes no user or device is trustworthy by default, even inside the network perimeter. Every access request is verified explicitly before granting access, following the principle of least privilege.

SSL/TLS encryption secures data transmitted between web browsers and servers. HTTPS uses TLS to encrypt HTTP traffic, protecting sensitive information such as login credentials and payment details.

A DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) is a physical or logical subnetwork that contains and exposes an organization's external-facing services to an untrusted network, usually the internet. It adds an extra layer of protection to the internal network.

Port scanning is a technique used to discover open ports and services on a target host. Defending against port scanning involves closing unused ports, using firewalls, and employing network segmentation.

DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks overwhelm a target with traffic from multiple compromised systems. Mitigation strategies include traffic filtering, rate limiting, content delivery networks, and upstream traffic scrubbing.
